:::{#exm-cosine-decay}
#### Cosine decay over a fixed run

Take $\iterpoint{\steplen}{0} = 0.1$ and $\schedlen = 90$.
The [step length](#def-cosine-decay) at $t = 0, 15, 45, 75, 90$ is:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: cosine-decay-r
#| code-fold: false
s0_cd <- 0.1
tau_cd <- 90
t_cd <- c(0, 15, 45, 75, 90)
angle_cd <- pi * t_cd / tau_cd
step_cd <- s0_cd / 2 * (1 + cos(angle_cd))
tibble::tibble(t = t_cd, step_length = step_cd)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: cosine-decay-python
#| code-fold: false
import math

s0_cd, tau_cd = 0.1, 90
for t_cd in [0, 15, 45, 75, 90]:
    print(t_cd, round(s0_cd / 2 * (1 + math.cos(math.pi * t_cd / tau_cd)), 6));
```

:::

The step length is $0.1$ at the start, half of that at $t = 45$, and zero at $t = 90$.
It changes slowly near both ends and fastest in the middle.

<!-- no-figure: the example tabulates five step lengths -->

:::
